clue.text: Players abide by this whistle on the ground

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece written on another comes after it

parts.note: a sports ground or field of play is a pitch
a pipe is a simple whistle-like wind instrument

explanation.surface: Footballers obey the referee's whistle out on the field of play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' suggests sportsmen, but the definition means musicians or singers, who take their note from this small instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicians and choirs tune to the note sounded by this small reed instrument.

clue.text: Goat found in the same place, formerly

parts.note: ib., short for ibidem, is the Latin reference note meaning in the same place
ex- means former or formerly, as in ex-wife

explanation.surface: A goat turns up where it used to be found.
explanation.walkthrough: IB (ibidem) is the footnote abbreviation scholars use for a source already cited.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild mountain species with long curved horns, found in the Alps.

clue.text: Brave Watch Co. gone bust…

indicators.note: a firm that has gone bust has broken up, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A watchmaking company bravely carries on after going bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective but is a noun: a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a Native American people from the south-eastern United States, so a warrior of that nation is a brave.

clue.text: … fence turning white, receiving last of jewels

parts.note: someone going white in the face is paling

indicators.note: the final letter of the word jewels is taken

explanation.surface: A fence goes pale on taking delivery of a final batch of stolen jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fence' suggests a receiver of stolen goods, which the word 'receiving' supports; here it is a row of stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointed stakes set in a row make a wooden barrier around a field.

clue.text: Long piece of wood?

explanation.surface: A plank described as lengthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn or long for something is one sense; the other is softwood timber from an evergreen tree.

clue.text: Meeting at which strikers are cheered

definitions.text: Meeting at which strikers are cheered

parts.words: Meeting at which strikers are cheered
parts.note: strikers suggests a rally of workers on strike, but they are goal-scoring forwards applauded by fans at a game

explanation.surface: A rally where striking workers are applauded.
explanation.definitionFit: A game between two teams where crowds cheer the forwards who score goals.

clue.text: Chronic patient?

parts.note: a chronic patient is ill for a long time; the phrase also means patient in temperament, enduring trouble without complaint

explanation.surface: A hospital patient with a lasting condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who endures hardship or annoyance without complaint for a great while.

clue.text: Part of town for noodle detachment?

indicators.note: a detachment separates things, so the letters are broken apart and reset

explanation.surface: A district set aside for a group of noodle-eaters.
explanation.walkthrough: The fortress is a part of London, the town; 'detachment' also hints at the soldiers garrisoned there.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic castle beside the Thames is a landmark district of the capital.

clue.text: Wash hairpiece -it reduces the highlights

parts.note: to dip something is to plunge or wash it in liquid, as sheep are dipped
a switch is a tress of false hair

explanation.surface: Rinse a wig, which tones down blonde streaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highlights' suggests hair colouring, but it means a car's headlights on full beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A car control that lowers the headlamp beam from full to dipped.

clue.text: Wild-eyed satyr of most recent history

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run riot and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A satyr with a crazed look from the very recent past.
explanation.definitionFit: The day before today is the latest stretch of the past.

clue.text: Letter from Cypriot abroad

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Correspondence from a Cypriot living overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: The way a person follows Beryl, for example

indicators.note: the word for a person comes after the word for the way

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
one means a person, as in no one

explanation.surface: A man trails after a woman called Beryl.
explanation.walkthrough: Beryl looks like a woman's name, but it is a mineral used as a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Beryl is a gem mineral, and gems are precious minerals of this kind.

clue.text: Fuzzy, light of head? It's a fever!

indicators.note: lighter by its head means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: vague means fuzzy or unclear

explanation.surface: Feeling woolly and light-headed is a sign of fever.
explanation.definitionFit: A malarial illness with bouts of shivering and high temperature.

clue.text: Fellow secure in flight …

parts.note: to lock something is to secure it

explanation.surface: A man fastened in during an aeroplane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' means a group of birds flying together, not an air journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of birds in the air together is a flight, as with geese or pigeons.

clue.text: … but silly Annie is insecure

indicators.note: insecure means unsteady or not fixed, so the name's letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A silly woman named Annie lacks confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolish and empty of sense.

clue.text: Everybody in to view a flat

indicators.note: the word for everybody goes inside the word for putting on view

parts.note: to show is to put on view
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Everyone is invited along to look round an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' suggests an apartment, but it means lacking depth or interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking depth, whether of water, feeling or thought.

clue.text: Children's outfitter might have sold one for a tanner

definitions.text: Children's outfitter might have sold one for a tanner

parts.words: Children's outfitter might have sold one for a tanner
parts.note: a tanner was old British slang for a sixpence coin, but also someone who tans in the sun

explanation.surface: A children's clothes shop once sold an item for sixpence.
explanation.definitionFit: A light child's garment worn for sunbathing on the beach.

clue.text: Criminal, bad here in France, gets time

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill luck
ici is French for here

explanation.surface: A villain behaving badly in France does time.
explanation.definitionFit: Against the law, unlawful.

clue.text: Producing heat that lifts balloons

explanation.surface: Hot air carries balloons upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat-related, as in heat-generating; also a rising current of warm air that carries balloons and gliders aloft.

clue.text: Fir-cone producer?

parts.note: a producer of cones is a cone-bearing tree, the kind that includes firs

explanation.surface: What makes fir cones?
explanation.definitionFit: A cone-bearing tree such as a fir, pine or spruce.

clue.text: Whitewash is finished in sporting competition

indicators.note: the word for finished goes inside the word for competition

parts.note: a cup is a sporting competition, such as the FA Cup
over means finished

explanation.surface: A cricket thrashing ends a knockout tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whitewash' suggests a total sporting defeat; here it is a concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: Concealing a scandal or wrongdoing to protect reputations.

clue.text: Guy's chilblain

explanation.surface: A man has a sore on his foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow or bloke; also a crack or sore in skin made rough by cold.

clue.text: The French hail and farewell

parts.note: le is French for the
ave is Latin for hail, a greeting

explanation.surface: French greetings and goodbyes.
explanation.walkthrough: AVE, as in Ave Maria, is a Latin greeting; 'farewell' is the leave one takes when departing.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking leave of someone is bidding them goodbye.

clue.text: In favour of Malay boat?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'In favour of Malay boat?': PRO (in favour of) is clear but no word supplies the final A; a word such as 'a' seems lost from the print.

clue.text: Art movement's pop article

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Dad's an art movement in himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' suggests Pop Art, but it is a father.
explanation.definitionFit: An early twentieth-century anti-art avant-garde style.

clue.text: Charity begins at home" feature

indicators.note: the clue says the word Charity begins, so take only its opening letter

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: The saying that charity begins at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is split up: 'begins' takes the start of 'Charity', and 'at home' is IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Part of the face below the mouth, one of the facial features.

clue.text: Warmonger of lesser degree can make one totter, say

definitions.text: Warmonger of lesser degree can make one totter, say

parts.words: Warmonger of lesser degree can make one totter, say
parts.note: a minor warmonger deals in small fights or scraps; a totter is a British rag-and-bone collector of junk

explanation.surface: A small-time aggressor can make his victim stagger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Totter' looks like a verb, to stagger; it is a noun for a dealer in discarded goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in junk metal and waste, and a scrap is also a fight.

clue.text: Law-breaker irregularly running off and hiding

indicators.note: breaking the law shatters the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: loping is running with a long, uneven bounding stride

explanation.surface: A criminal runs off and goes into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding' looks like concealment but means a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe beating or thrashing, as in giving someone a good hiding.
